title: I Borrowed $3k From Affirm. Here's How It's Going.
summary: Personal update video from an Affirm user showing a paid-off, zero-interest loan history.

assertions.quote: both of my loans... zero percent interest... there's literally no downside

verdicts.note: This is the standard, verifiable structure of the interest-free pay-in-four product when used as designed.
CFPB's executive summary describes BNPL as splitting a retail transaction 'into smaller, interest-free installments,' repaid as agreed with no interest added to the item's price.

assertions.quote: whenever you buy something you could shop at different places and then... choose a firm
by splitting it up into smaller payments... I have more breathing room to pay for rent and my car payments

verdicts.note: Splitting payments can ease a single month's cash flow, but this benefit is undercut when a user stacks multiple simultaneous loans.

assertions.quote: if the interest rate is super high then that's a different story

verdicts.note: Providers' own disclosures describe offering both 0% and interest-bearing terms depending on the applicant's creditworthiness.

FEDS Notes: users with credit scores below 620 were less likely to cite avoiding interest as a reason for using BNPL than higher-score users, which the authors call 'puzzling' given lower-score borrowers would likely face higher rates.
